title: Fynaptix · Robotics Research
heading: Robotics Sector Intelligence
subheading: Deep-research edition · trends, tiers, catalysts & risks
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — it is not a personalized recommendation to buy or sell any security. Robotics and humanoid names are volatile and many trade at premium valuations; private company valuations are illustrative and not directly investable. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Unmanned systems & counter-drone budget — defense-robotics tailwind

themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Tesla, Figure, Apptronik, 1X, Agility, Unitree racing to scale. ~18k units shipped 2025 (+508%), but still pre-mass-commercialization; most revenue is pilots.

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Most commercially mature sub-sector. Symbotic's ~$22.7B backlog proves automation is generating real cash today; Amazon's reported multi-billion warehouse-robotics buildout validates the category.

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: ISRG dominant (Q2 revenue $2.89B, +19% YoY, beat estimates) but stock -25%+ YTD as multiples compress; J&J Ottava met bariatric pivotal-study endpoints, Medtronic Hugo cleared for urology.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: AVAV (~$1.1B funded backlog), KTOS (+72% YTD on Valkyrie/CCA), private Anduril (~$61B val. after $5B May raise, $20B Army contract). Pentagon FY27 budget requests ~$75B for unmanned/counter-drone systems.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: Deere put its first autonomous articulated dump truck to work in a quarry (2nd-gen autonomy kit); Caterpillar unveiled a five-machine autonomous construction lineup.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Fanuc and Keyence hit limit-up on FY27 double-digit profit guidance + buyback; rally spread to Yaskawa and SMC despite near-term FA demand deceleration.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: Actuators/reducers (Harmonic Drive), motion control (Regal Rexnord), vision (Cognex +69.9% 6mo, EPS +112.5%), rare earths (MP Materials). Sells to every OEM — leveraged to build rates, not to which humanoid wins.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA launched an open Isaac GR00T reference humanoid (Unitree H2 Plus chassis + Jetson Thor compute) for research labs, shipping via Unitree late 2026. Foundation-model startups (Skild AI now ~$14B val., Physical Intelligence reportedly near $11B) raising billions to be the software layer.

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Q2 2026 China humanoid investment surged 6x YoY to ~$6.9B; Unitree (STAR listing approved, ~$14.7B val.), Agibot, LimX ($2.2B pre-IPO) all rushing to list. Price war risk: Unitree R1 humanoid at $5,900.

bear_case.title: Bubble warnings from serious sources
bear_case.description: China's NDRC has warned of a humanoid "bubble" — capital flooding in while verified applications remain scarce. Morgan Stanley flags a wide gap between hype and scalability; some VCs compare the setup to the dotcom era.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Dexterity, inference speed, reliability, and cost still confine real use to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: Fundamentals already diverging
bear_case.description: Unitree's Q1 2026 profit fell 52% YoY even as its IPO was approved; ISRG fell 25%+ YTD despite beating Q2 earnings; drone stocks stayed choppy despite record backlogs. Multiples, not fundamentals, are doing the work in parts of the sector.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. Component and warehouse names carry less thesis risk than humanoid pure-plays.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: Unitree's $5,900 R1 signals aggressive price compression that could squeeze Western OEM margins before the market matures.

bear_case.title: "Dot-com stage" warnings
bear_case.description: KB Securities likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble, noting robotics and space names saw the sharpest volatility during May's market turbulence. Sector EV/EBITDA multiples hit 16.8x in Q4 2025, ranging from 0.9x (mature industrials) to 78.2x (speculative pure-plays) — a valuation split investors should not treat as one trade.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Symbotic
positions.note: ~$22.7B backlog means the automation thesis is already generating cash rather than promising it in 2030.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Isaac GR00T and Jetson Thor make it the default robot brain — but it is also the largest name in your AI sleeve, so check total exposure before adding here.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: Dominant installed base, Q2 revenue +19% YoY. The -25% YTD de-rating is what makes it interesting; the growth was never in question.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: Machine vision sells into every OEM regardless of which humanoid wins. EPS +112.5% and it is not priced as an AI name.

positions.name: Rockwell Automation
positions.note: The cleanest listed US factory-automation exposure, at a valuation that does not require humanoids to work.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Optimus is the largest humanoid option available in public markets — attached to a car business carrying its own capex warning. You are not buying a robotics pure-play.

positions.name: Harmonic Drive
positions.note: Pure leverage to humanoid build rates via actuators and reducers. Small, illiquid and awkward to access from the UK.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: ~$1.1B funded backlog. Overlaps directly with your Defense sleeve — own it in one place, not both.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: +72% YTD on Valkyrie and CCA. The story is fully priced; the execution is not yet proven.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: Sidewalk delivery at real unit economics is unproven and the cash burn is continuous. Size it to go to zero.

positions.name: Deere & Co
positions.note: The autonomy kit is real and revenue-generating, but robotics is a rounding error next to the ag cycle you would actually be buying.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: Five-machine autonomous lineup announced — same problem as Deere: construction demand dominates the return.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Limit-up on FY27 guidance and a buyback. The re-rating has happened; the FA demand recovery has not.

positions.name: Keyence
positions.note: Exceptional margins and permanently expensive. Needs a genuine de-rating before the maths works.

positions.name: ABB Ltd
positions.note: Selling the robotics division to SoftBank for $5.375B — which removes most of the reason it was on this list.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Magnet supply matters more than any single robot maker, but it sits in your Critical Minerals sleeve. Do not double-count it.

positions.name: Teradyne
positions.note: Universal Robots is still small against semi test. This is a semiconductor-cycle bet wearing a robotics label.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: RPA is being disrupted by the same AI agents it claims to ride, and the robotics label is marketing rather than hardware.

positions.name: Ouster
positions.note: Lidar remains a commodity price war with no evidence of durable margin at any of the listed players.
